topic.title: What lies under the streets of Paris: the Catacombs' walls of bones, the Metro under the Ile de la Cite, the long spiral stair at Abbesses and the new deep Line 15 station

title: What's Hidden Under the Streets of Paris?
description:
What's hidden under the streets of Paris? Bones, the Metro, a long spiral stair and a station that hasn't opened yet.
The layers are from different parts of Paris, stacked in one cutaway.
Sources: Catacombes de Paris, Wikipedia, Sortiraparis (Nov 2026).
Depths from published sources. Cutaway illustrations, not to scale.
cta: Rome or London: which city should we dive under next? Comment

lines.text: What's hidden under the streets of Paris, and how deep does it go?
20 m down, the Catacombs: walls of stacked bones.
Deeper, 25 m: the Metro, under an island in the Seine.
At Abbesses, 36 m down, a spiral stair of 176 steps.
And 52 m down, a Line Fifteen station not open yet.
But those bones up top? 6M people.
All still under the streets of Paris.

Beat line15: 'And 52 m down sits a new Line Fifteen station.' with the moment 'a train glides in' presents Saint-Maur-Creteil as an open, running station. It is not open: Line 15 South slipped to autumn 2027 (Wikipedia Paris Metro Line 15: 'planned to open in autumn 2027'; Societe des grands projets notice, June 2026, pushed commissioning to autumn 2027). The topic's verify list requires saying 'being built' or 'opened'. Fix: say it is still being built (e.g. 'And 52 m down, a Line Fifteen station still being built.') and drop the arriving passenger train (an empty hall or a test train is fine). The 52 m depth itself is confirmed (Sortiraparis 282604: '52 metres underground'; Wikipedia station table agrees).

All other facts confirmed: Catacombs 20 m (catacombes.paris.fr: 'Twenty meters underground'); 6M people (official site says 'several million'; 'more than six million' per Wikipedia, also National Geographic and Smithsonian report ~six million, so OK); Cite 25 m, Abbesses 36 m and 176 steps (Sortiraparis 280379, page shows all three; RATP page 403, so 36 m said as 'down' from street level per verify, which the line does); no 'deepest' claim made; description carries the disclaimer and says the layers are stacked from different parts of Paris; no entry details for closed quarries.

Beat line15 (re-review): 'And 52 m down, a Line Fifteen station is still being dug.' with 'the boring machine cutterhead turns' is false today. Tunnelling on Line 15 South ended in December 2021 (Societe du Grand Paris: TBM Marina arrived at Creteil-l'Echat on 20 Dec 2021, completing the 37 km tunnel); track was laid by end 2023 and the line is now in test running, with opening slipped to autumn 2027 (Wikipedia Paris Metro Line 15; SGP notice June 2026). Fix: say it is built but not yet open, e.g. 'And 52 m down, a Line Fifteen station that hasn't opened yet.' and show a finished but empty hall (a driverless test train is fine); no boring machine, no digging.
All other facts stay confirmed as in the first review (20 m, 6M, 25 m, 36 m, 176 steps, 52 m depth; disclaimer present).
